question: A 30-year-old man (index case) affected by Leber's optic atrophy presents the mutation of the mitochondrial genome LHON11778A. In genetic counseling you will be informed of the risks of transmitting the disease to your offspring. What information is correct?

options.opa: The index case will transmit the disease to all its male descendants (holándrica inheritance).
options.opb: The disease will be transmitted to 50% of the descendants of the index case, regardless of their sex.
options.opc: The disease will be transmitted to all descendants of the index case, as it is of paternal inheritance.
options.opd: The disease will be transmitted to female descendants; but to no man.
options.ope: The disease will not be transmitted to the descendants of the index case, because it is of maternal inheritance.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: LHON11778A mutation in mitochondrial genome -> Leber's optic atrophy in the index case -> genetic risk for offspring -> uncertain inheritance pattern -> 50% confidence. CHAIN: LHON11778A mutation -> Leber's optic atrophy -> genetic counseling -> inheritance pattern evaluation -> holándrica inheritance -> 20% confidence. CHAIN: LHON11778A mutation -> Leber's optic atrophy -> genetic counseling -> inheritance pattern assessment -> paternal inheritance -> 50%
enhanced_information: The correct information is that the disease will be transmitted to all descendants of the index case, as it is of maternal inheritance. This is supported by the LHON11778A mutation in the mitochondrial genome, leading to Leber's optic atrophy, which is maternally inherited.
analysis: Leber's optic atrophy associated with the LHON11778A mutation in the mitochondrial genome is inherited maternally. Mitochondrial DNA is passed down from the mother to all offspring, so the disease will be transmitted to all descendants of the index case.
